The model and memory floors are unchanged. RTX 3090 remains deferred; upstream engine merge remains deferred (EXP-065).

interpretation: The RTX 4090 change is idle-to-new-session latency, not a decode-kernel speedup: C1 is 157.90 tok/s at 87.59% MTP acceptance against v0.6.8's 157.89. EXP-064 found 0.29-0.47 s prefill after 12-58 s idle without keep-warm and rejected the RTX 5090's 3.5 ms/10 ms spin on this card. EXP-066's sm_89 50 ms/100 ms spin holds P2: post-idle prefill 0.1461-0.1481 s, TTFT 0.167-0.178 s, all 31 outputs byte-identical, at about 72 W above idle while held. A request arriving mid-spin can overlap one warp for up to 50 ms. The canonical v0.6.9 package passed 130,048-token exact retrieval in 91.0 s, managed-stop flush, both rollback directions versus v0.6.8, security and an OMP 18.3.5 typed tool turn. EXP-064's issue_48_field_start passed from the refusing memory state with the published v0.6.8 package; a recurrence still reports commit limit, available commit and available memory. RTX 5090 runtime qualification is unchanged, and its v0.8.3 checkpoints carry across; RTX 4090 checkpoints from v0.6.8 are incompatible with the changed server build and each session re-prefills once. EXP-067 proves one short stock OMP 18.3.5 session per lane survives graceful restarts, using the macOS arm64 binary only; that proof is separate from the passed documented-route and client-platform acceptance. All four routes passed on candidate 68302298, and the upstream macOS arm64 (preview), Windows x64 and Linux x64 binaries each passed a typed tool turn, exact continuation and fail-closed request against image cd9e10b1 (releases/v0.8.4/acceptance/composed-external-installation.json); Linux ran under WSL2, not a separately qualified Linux OS. Both hosts were restored (docs/measurements/2026-09-28-v084-acceptance-restoration.json). EXP-065 keeps the upstream engine merge deferred: e31bc99b has a 1.5% single-run prefill lead, already present in EXP-048, but about 18% slower decode rounds and weaker reuse. Owner-operated exact-profile scope only; no SLA or universal warm-reuse claim.
